data.one_liner: Untagged union types using Dart extension types.
data.what_it_does: Provides generic extension types (Union2 through Union9) to represent untagged union types in Dart with zero runtime overhead. Offers split methods to pattern match and handle each operand safely.
use_when: You need to restrict a function parameter to a specific set of types (e.g., int or String) without creating custom wrapper classes.
You want compile-time type safety for union values with zero runtime allocation cost.
avoid_when: You require traditional algebraic property support like subtyping and order-independence out of the box.
You want implicit constructor syntax which is not yet supported natively by Dart.
strengths: Zero runtime overhead because it leverages Dart extension types.
Provides static type checks for handling union cases via split methods.
Includes a bounded variant for improved run-time type safety.
weaknesses: Lacks traditional algebraic properties and implicit constructors.
Extension types can have their encapsulation violated via manual type casts.
